doc.title: George Russell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Hospital, Miles Davis and Gil Evans
title: Dating his second, longer hospital stay
summary: They try to date the 15-month second hospitalization, placing it c. 1945-46, between Benny Carter and Dizzy.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: That ’47. Let’s pull – can we pull back for a second? It’s my understanding you got sick again, and this time you were in the hospital for a much longer time. You said six months the first time.
15 months? Now, what period are we talking about?
As I said, I went to New York. I went through all of this – I was in the hospital – when was that? That had to be – I’m not so sure, but I know it was 15 months. It had to be from . . .
I don’t want to put words in your mouth.

No, I don’t want to do that, but the dates I’ve seen most often aren’t specific, but they usually say ’45 into ’46, which would make sense, since it’s 15 months. It’s certainly longer than a year. We know you were with Benny in ’44. Then we know you were with Diz in ’47.
So it’s kind of like a – you had never really healed. You had been ushered out of the hospital, you and Gaston and others.
